decision: Spend recorded in USD; one display currency per install with an admin-set exchange rate; budgets entered and shown in it
Exchange rates are set by hand in release 1; an opt-in automatic daily rate comes after release 1
Each environment names default models (one per API format, optional small model); sekisho use writes them
Environment labels, such as a cost centre, travel with spend exports (FOCUS tags), kept per spend record

Remaining market-research items placed: R1 default model and labels; R2 rate limits, CI OIDC, egress, sandbox and approval modes, review diff and signatures, MCP Registry source; R3 inventory export, usage per entry, SIEM, CIBA; not planned: forecasts, tool search, Agent Trace
Bedrock and Azure providers serve the Anthropic or the OpenAI route, chosen per provider; Claude on Azure Foundry needs Entra credentials (plan 1b)

Refusing built-in-provider models the catalog can't price stays in plan 6
The gateway's cloud identity, AWS access keys and Entra service principals only go to AWS or Azure hosts
regex: only go to AWS or Azure hosts

decision: Changing where a provider's requests go (base URL, region, endpoint) needs its credential again
Azure providers are set up by the endpoint URL the Azure portal shows
Provider base URLs are checked for private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses when saved; private ones need allow_private_network
Plan 8's Helm chart blocks cloud metadata addresses from agentgateway
Recorded spend stays close to the provider's bill (plan 1c)
A stream that ends early is charged an estimate: the provider's counts where reported, the prompt from agentgateway's tokenizer, the answer from the text that reached the client
An admin's prices win over agentgateway's catalog whatever model name the provider reports
Model prices have four parts (input, output, cache read, cache write), with the provider's usual ratios as defaults
A model without an admin price keeps agentgateway's catalog cost; Sekisho keeps a copy of the catalog to price estimates (our call)
The rate-limit service answers at once and records spend on a task of its own (our call)
Each estimated charge is logged; a request with no price anywhere is logged as a warning (our call)
A stream agentgateway never reports is charged its estimate by the rate-limit service once the stream hook's tally ends; a later report is refused (our call)
A stream that ended before any answer reached the client (agentgateway's own error) is charged nothing (our call)
regex: before any answer reached the client

decision: Session tokens are checked by Sekisho's extAuthz on model routes, not by agentgateway's jwtAuth, and extAuthz names the person each charge goes to (our call, plan 2)
Session tokens are Ed25519 JWTs; signing keys rotate every 30 days and on demand; a new key is published a minute before it signs (our call)
Refresh tokens rotate on every use; a session ends after 30 days without a refresh; a rotated token presented again ends the session, except within 10 s (our call)
One Dex refresh token per user, shared by their sessions, replayed under a lock on a task the client can't cancel (our call, from ACH)
regex: one Dex refresh token per user

decision: A daily check at Dex of every owner of an active environment key (our call, from ACH)
Dex's sessions_enabled stays off; only api_connectors_crud is on; Dex sign-ins end by RevokeRefresh (our call)
Sekisho registers itself as a client of Dex through Dex's gRPC API (our call)
regex: registers itself as a client of Dex

decision: Users are matched by Dex's subject or a local account's Dex user ID, never linked by email (our call, as Obot)
regex: never links? accounts by email|never linked by email

decision: Sekisho groups can hold any user; Dex's connectors set which upstream claim carries groups (our call)
regex: Sekisho groups can hold any user

decision: Admins by mark or SEKISHO_ADMIN_GROUPS, read live; environment access only through access groups, no implicit access for admins (our call)
The bootstrap token only creates the first admin on /setup; sekisho admin-link recovers a lost admin (our call, as Obot)
Setup links work once for 7 days; passwords of 12 characters to 72 bytes, bcrypt at cost 12 for Dex; a reset ends the person's sessions (our call)
Environment owners arrive in plan 2 with offboarding; catalog entries' owners stay in plan 3
Offboarding disables the person and hands everything to one new owner; users are disabled, never deleted, in release 1 (our call)
A key is invalid while its owner is disabled, refused at Dex or outside the access groups, and works again once access returns (our call)
Keys are created by their owner; admins list, suspend, resume and revoke anyone's keys (our call)
OAuth details: 60 s codes with PKCE S256, 10-minute device codes, the pre-registered sekisho-cli client with loopback redirects (our call)
Dex's gRPC port is never published; browsers reach Dex at its issuer, Sekisho over the private network (our call)
Every coding tool reaches an environment's A2A agents as tools on its MCP endpoint, served by Sekisho and relayed over A2A (decided 2026-11-12)
Gemini CLI's own remote-agent files for A2A agents are placed in release 2 (our call)
Every local MCP server names an exact package version or image digest; an entry without one is refused at sync (decided 2026-11-12)
How local MCP servers are pinned: Obot's three runtimes only, npm @version and Python == or @, container tags resolved to digests at sync, plugins' MCP servers checked too (our call)
Dex's HTTP 500 at refresh is unavailable, never a refusal: with Dex v2.46.1 the daily check catches only dead Dex tokens, leavers are offboarded in Sekisho (decided 2026-11-12)
Each A2A agent's MCP tool has a name of its own on the environment's MCP endpoint (our call)
An A2A agent's MCP tool goes through the same checks as the A2A route: access, the caller's identity and the call's record, once (our call)
regex: same checks as the A2A route

decision: Long A2A tasks: progress at least every 30 seconds, an MCP task for clients that declare the MCP tasks extension and a plain call for the rest, resubscribe or GetTask after a dropped stream (our call)
A2A answers keep non-text parts: data parts as JSON, files as MCP resource links or embedded resources (our call)
